evidence.title: Flying Gold
evidence.text: Flying Gold (Hungarian: Repülő arany or Repülö arany) is a 1932 Hungarian crime film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Steven Geray, Gyula Kabos and Lajos Gárday.

evidence.title: Flying Gold
evidence.text: A shipment of gold being flown from Paris to Budapest is robbed in mid-air.

evidence.title: Steve Sekely
evidence.text: Steve Sekely (1899-1979) was a Hungarian film director.

evidence.title: Steve Sekely
evidence.text: Born Székely István, he was known by several names, based on his changing professional and immigration status, including Stefan Szekely.

evidence.title: King Baggot
evidence.text: William King Baggot (November 7, 1879 – July 11, 1948) was an American actor, film director and screenwriter.

evidence.title: King Baggot
evidence.text: He was an internationally famous movie star of the silent film era.

evidence.title: King Baggot
evidence.text: The first individually publicized leading man in America, Baggot was referred to as "King of the Movies," "The Most Photographed Man in the World" and "The Man Whose Face Is As Familiar As The Man In The Moon."

evidence.title: The Fabulous Suzanne
evidence.text: The Fabulous Suzanne is a 1946 American romantic comedy film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Barbara Britton, Rudy Vallee and Otto Kruger.

evidence.title: The Fabulous Suzanne
evidence.text: A waitress inherits a fortune from one of her customers.

evidence.title: Number 111 (1938 film)
evidence.text: Number 111 is a 1938 Hungarian thriller film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Jenő Törzs, Pál Jávor and Mária Lázár.

evidence.title: Number 111 (1938 film)
evidence.text: It is a remake of the 1919 film "Number 111", directed by Alexander Korda, which was itself an adaptation of a novel by Jenő Heltai.

evidence.title: Cafe Moscow
evidence.text: Cafe Moscow (Hungarian:Café Moszkva) is a 1936 Hungarian adventure film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Anna Tõkés, Gyula Csortos and Ferenc Kiss.

evidence.title: Cafe Moscow
evidence.text: Art direction was by József Pán.

evidence.title: Cafe Moscow
evidence.text: It is also known by the alternative title Only One Night.

evidence.title: Cafe Moscow
evidence.text: The film is set during the First World War on the Eastern Front between Russia and the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

evidence.title: Cafe Moscow
evidence.text: The film was intended to convey an anti-war message.

evidence.title: A Tremendously Rich Man
evidence.text: A Tremendously Rich Man (German: Ein steinreicher Mann) is a 1932 German comedy film directed by Steve Sekely and starring Curt Bois, Dolly Haas and Adele Sandrock.

evidence.title: A Tremendously Rich Man
evidence.text: It premiered on 13 February 1932.

evidence.title: A Tremendously Rich Man
evidence.text: The film was a co-production between the German subsidiary of Universal Pictures and the German firm Tobis Film.
